body:
DESIGN-STAGE. Deliverable is a working spec at `.adlc/specs/NN-law-resolution.md` plus answered design questions, then STOP for Myk's word before implementation.

RAISED BY MYK (2026-07-25, in chat), reframing the T33 root-name guard: "Schemas are derived from deltas like everything else. Meaning that, just as anywhere else in this system, what feels like a conflict is actually just data, it's something to be resolved at the appropriate layer within a lens configuration. It sounds like what you're saying is that somewhere there's a hard-coded MOST_RECENT policy making some assumptions."

There is. Two of them:

1. `loadHyperSchema` (rhizomatic `schema-deltas.ts:73-84`) takes the latest surviving definition at an entity by claimed timestamp, lexById tiebreak — and its OWN comment calls that "a policy choice". rhizomatic is frozen; this pick is not ours to edit.
2. `readRegistrations` (`src/gateway/registration.ts:725-737`) keys latest-per-(registration entity, lens name) with `latest.set(...)` — "ground order: last write wins". Ours, and equally unconfigurable.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. Data resolution runs through a Schema whose Policies are first-class and configurable (`pick`/`all`/`merge`/`conflicts`/`absentAs`, ordered `byTimestamp` or `byAuthorRank`) — that IS the paradigm. Law resolution has no policy layer at all, so "which of my thousand overlapping Posts binds" is decided by a timestamp comparison nobody configured and no reader can see.

This is also the mechanism behind T33's entity-capture defect (PR #210): a module row pointing at the root's own `hyperschema:Plant` with a large timestamp made an operator-signed definition win latest-wins at the operator's own entity. T33 shipped a door-time refusal, which is a fail-fast patch over a missing resolution layer — and it cannot help at all when law arrives by FEDERATION, where no door runs.

THE SHAPE, and why it needs no rhizomatic change: Loam controls the OPERAND SET it hands `loadHyperSchema`/`loadSchema` (`lawfulSnapshot`). Narrow that set to what a policy chose and rhizomatic's latest-of-one is trivially that choice — the bootstrap stays untouched. (T33's own audit found this same lever: author scoping had to reach the operand set, because the bootstrap mask is author-blind one layer down.)

DESIGN QUESTIONS (each with a reasoned recommendation):
1. What is the policy's at-rest form? A `loam.lawpolicy`-shaped declaration per lens name (or store-wide with per-lens override)? Reuse rhizomatic's Policy vocabulary verbatim, or a smaller closed set for law?
2. Which orders must be sayable? At minimum: `latest` (today's default, so no migration and no behavior change until configured), a provenance rank (law I published directly outranks law I adopted — the T33 case, expressible because adoption records exist), and `conflicts`.
3. What does `conflicts` MEAN for law? Recommendation: the lens binds NOTHING and surfaces a named defect — an unbound lens is honest, a coin-flip lens is not. Confirm, because it means a store can be configured into serving less.
4. Does the policy resolve law at every reader, or only at the registration read? Name every site (`readRegistrations`, `readRenderers` latest-per-route, binding definitions in the runner, `readTranslations`) — the one-rule-N-sites hazard is live here, and §21/§23.5's living-name semantics are the same shape.
5. What happens to T33's door guard? Recommendation: keep it as the fail-fast refusal (it stops a bad mint before provenance is written) but stop treating it as the answer — federation has no door, so the policy is the general case.
6. Is a store with no declaration byte-identical to today? It must be.

RAILS the spec should name: a store with no policy declaration resolves exactly as today (object level, at the door); a provenance-ranked policy makes the T33 capture impossible BY RESOLUTION with the door guard disabled; `conflicts` leaves the lens unbound with the defect named; a federated definition with a huge timestamp does not win under a provenance policy (the case no door can catch); every named reader site honors the same policy (mutate the shared predicate and ALL sites go red).

CARE: this changes what decides whose law binds — a trust-model surface. Design-stage, so Myk's word before code and Myk's merge after. Edges: it supersedes the framing of T33's guard (already landed) and is adjacent to T37's constitutional-reads indexing, which touches the same readers.
title: Law resolution has no Policy — two hard-coded latest-wins picks decide whose schema binds
